figures.before: What Self-Perform Means in Construction: The GC Owns and Manages the Labor Directly
figures.alt: Concrete pour preparation with rebar, vapor barrier, edge forms, and a clean ready-to-place slab area
figures.caption: Self-perform work means the GC controls the labor, tools, sequence, quality checks, production plan, safety, and handoff to the trades that follow rather than only brokering that scope.

figures.before: How JK Vets and Manages Subcontracted Trades
figures.alt: Contractor qualification documents, insurance verification, and a blank checklist organized on a clean desk
figures.caption: Subcontracted work still needs active management. Qualification, scope, insurance, schedule, submittals, field coordination, inspections, quality, and closeout are part of the GC’s responsibility.

figures.before: How to Evaluate a GC's Self-Perform Claim
figures.alt: Construction planning table with drawings, measuring tools, a blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: The question is not whether a contractor uses a broad label. It is which scopes they control, how those scopes affect the critical path, and how the responsibility is documented in the project plan.
